The July 31, 2024 FOMC communication remains cautiously optimistic on growth and disinflation, but retains a high bar for easing: the target range stays at 5.25–5.50 percent, interest on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, and quantitative tightening continues via capped roll-offs ($25 billion Treasuries, $35 billion agency MBS) alongside standing repo/reverse repo facilities to maintain control of short rates. The “greater confidence” criterion underscores an expectations-management approach to ensure inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent before cuts.

Incorporating the Financial Stability Report lens tempers the tone. While banking stresses have stabilized since late 2023 and certain securitization segments recovered in 2024, vulnerabilities persist: CRE (especially office) remains under pressure; market liquidity can strain under stress; higher long-term rates and fiscal debt concerns keep term premia elevated; leverage in parts of the nonbank sector and tight bank lending standards pose downside risks; and Treasury market functioning relies on robust backstops. These FSR-flagged risks support a cautious, risk-management stance and justify maintaining restrictive policy until disinflation is clearly durable.

Net assessment: modestly positive on activity and disinflation progress, but more constrained by financial-stability vulnerabilities than a purely macro read would suggest.
